subject: nepobabies
one_liner: A block-building game platform where every player starts at the finish line, because their parents already paid for the level.
brand_voice_notes: Old-money private club voice applied to a children's block game. Speaks like a family office describing a trust fund: calm, discreet, faintly bored. Never acknowledges that anything was unearned. Words like 'legacy', 'stewardship' and 'heir' are used about Robux. Contractors exist but are never named above the fold.

hero.h1: Everyone starts somewhere. You start at the end.
hero.sub: Spawnpoint is a block-building game platform for the children of people you have heard of. Every obby arrives pre-completed, every game ships with a founder credit in your name, and every Robux is held in trust until a grown-up signs for it.

features.title: Pre-completed obbies
features.blurb: Each obstacle course is finished by a licensed professional before you log in. You spawn on the final platform beside the trophy, and the badge is already in your inventory. Jumping is optional and, for liability reasons, discouraged.

features.title: The Robux Trust
features.blurb: Your in-game currency sits in an irrevocable trust administered by your father's business manager. Withdrawals need two signatures, neither of them yours. Interest compounds quarterly and is reported to your mother's accountant in Zurich.

features.title: Merit Mode
features.blurb: One toggle rewrites the credits on any game you own. You become Founder, Lead Designer and Visionary. The 41 contractors who built it move to a scrolling 'Special Thanks' panel set in 9-point type.

pricing_tiers.name: Gap Year
pricing_tiers.tagline: Covered by a parent. You will not see the invoice.
perks: Founder credit on up to 2 games

pricing_tiers.name: Legacy
pricing_tiers.tagline: For heirs with a podcast in development.
perks: A human contractor on call 06:00 to 23:00
Avatar fitted by a stylist who has dressed a Kardashian, once

pricing_tiers.name: Dynasty
pricing_tiers.tagline: We do not publish this number. Neither will you.
perks: A private server named after a wing of a museum
Front-page placement, regardless of player count
Board seat on the Spawnpoint Youth Advisory Council

testimonials.quote: I built my first game when I was nine. Well, it was built while I was nine. I was in the room for most of it.
testimonials.name: Tallulah Whitcombe-Ashford
testimonials.title: Founder & Visionary (age 11), Third-Generation Content Creator

testimonials.quote: Merit Mode changed how my teachers look at me. My dad made one phone call and the school now uses Spawnpoint in assembly.
testimonials.name: Bram Okonkwo-Vance
testimonials.title: Co-CEO of His Mother's Production Company, Grade 7

testimonials.quote: My son has 2.1 million visits on Yacht Tycoon: Monaco. I have not checked who made it and I am not going to.
testimonials.name: Graham Ashford
testimonials.title: Executive Producer, Ashford Pictures, and Father (Primary Signatory)

demo_screen_concept: The Heir Console: a dark creator dashboard for an 11-year-old founder. A left rail lists her games (Yacht Tycoon: Monaco, Polo Obby, Gala Simulator) with visit counts and a gold 'Founder' crest. Main panel has tabs: Experiences (cards with 'Skip to finish' buttons and a filter for 'built by me*'), Credits (a live credits roll with a Merit Mode toggle that slides 41 contractor names into a tiny Special Thanks box and promotes the heir to every title), and Robux Trust (balance, a quarterly-interest sparkline, and a 'Request withdrawal' modal that shows two pending approvers: Dad's business manager and Dad's other business manager, with an approval progress bar that never moves past 0 of 2). A search field finds avatar items, all tagged 'Already owned (inherited)'.

images.rationale: Hero used: the club-at-night direction is photographic and needs a staged product shot. Demo skipped: the Heir Console is a dashboard of credits, tabs and a trust balance, nothing photo-shaped. Testimonials: one headshot for the adult signatory (Graham Ashford); the two child founders keep the gold founder-crest monogram, which is on-motif. Budget used: 2 of 4.

items.prompt: Moody editorial still-life photograph: a single small plastic blocky toy figure, like a building-block game avatar, wearing a tiny navy blazer with a gold crest, standing alone on a white marble plinth inside a dark private members club at night. Deep bottle green leather wall #0E1612 behind, a warm brass club lamp casting a pool of light, brass hairline details #C8A24A, a hint of claret velvet rope #A3263A in the soft-focus foreground. Low key lighting, shallow depth of field, expensive and quiet. One focal subject. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens.

Deadpan corporate headshot photograph of a tanned silver-haired film producer in his late fifties, navy cashmere sweater over open-collar white shirt, faint smug half-smile, seated in a dark green leather club chair, background deep bottle green #0E1612 with a soft warm brass lamp glow #C8A24A, low-key editorial lighting, head and shoulders centred. One focal subject. No text, no letters, no numbers, no logos, no watermarks, no rendered UI screens.

design_direction.style: Dark private-members'-club game launcher, after-hours mode. A block-building game platform dressed as a gentlemen's club at night: deep bottle-green leather ground, brass hairlines, a high-contrast Didone display face, and toy building blocks rendered as flat studded tiles in gold and racing green. Explicitly absent, because the last seven entries used them: gum leaf corners, sleep rings, zzz chips, 3px ink outlines, hard offset shadows, tennis seams, amount pills, masonry pins, iridescent gradients, crumb trails, lip buttons, lesson paths, bone meters, mascots, wall labels, empty plinths, clay stacks, silk threads, exuvia outlines, LCD pixel greens, parts diagrams, warning boxes. Also absent: daylight backgrounds (this is the first dark ground in eight entries), glassmorphism, neon, pastel. Four motifs carry the page. (1) The stud tile: features and tiers sit on flat dark-green panels with a row of small circular brass studs along the top edge, like a toy brick seen from above. (2) The brass rule: 1px #C8A24A hairlines with a small diamond at the centre separate every section, like a club menu. (3) The founder crest: a gold monogram shield with a crown of three blocks, used as the logo, the testimonial badge and the 'Founder' tag in the demo. (4) The velvet rope: the primary CTA and the highlighted tier hang behind a small SVG rope swag in claret #A3263A, the only red on the page besides Roblox-style error states. Corners 4px on panels, 2px on buttons. Shadows: one soft 0 20px 40px at 40% black for lift, nothing else.
design_direction.archetype: Game platform / app launcher landing: hero with a staged product image, feature panels, testimonials as club member cards, pricing as three membership tiers, demo CTA as 'enter the lobby'.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Slow and expensive. Elements rise 12px and fade in over 500ms on scroll (gated on a .js class with a timeout fallback). Studs light up brass one by one on hover. The velvet rope sways 2 degrees on hover of the CTA. Respects prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Split hero on desktop: left column carries an uppercase brass eyebrow ('Members only. Est. by someone else.'), the Didone h1 at 72px with 'the end' in italic, the sub, and the roped CTA. Right column is a 16:9 photo of a single toy block figure in a tiny blazer standing on a marble plinth under a club lamp, framed by a 1px brass border with corner diamonds. Below the hero, a thin ticker of fake stats in mono: 'Obbies completed on members' behalf: 1,204,889'. Stacks on mobile with image first.
